summary: VH fails 3 hard gates. HYP-2 lacks falsification criteria, a new user group is introduced that does not exist in the PFD, and one hypothesis expands scope beyond the problem space.

blocking_issues.description: HYP-2 states 'users will find notifications more actionable' but provides no falsification criteria — no threshold, no measurement, no condition under which the hypothesis is considered false. A hypothesis without falsification criteria cannot be tested.

HYP-3 references 'Mobile-First Users' as a target group. No such user group (UG-N identifier) exists in PFD-TASKFLOW-NOTIF-001. User groups must be traced to PFD identifiers — new groups may not be introduced.

HYP-4 addresses 'cross-platform notification consistency across web, mobile, and Slack.' The PFD problem statement is scoped to the notification system's priority and role differentiation — cross-platform consistency is a distinct problem not present in the PFD.
